name: Dave Morin
category: Social platform product leader / startup founder
milestone_by_age_26: As Facebook senior platform manager, co-created Facebook Platform (public launch May 2007) enabling third-party apps inside Facebook, at age 26.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Helena, Montana, and skied for the northern division of the U.S. Junior Olympic team before studying economics at the University of Colorado Boulder (B.A. 2003). Joined Apple marketing in 2003, then moved to Facebook in 2006 as senior platform manager, helping build Platform and later Facebook Connect.
family_context_summary: Raised in Helena, Montana; competitive junior skiing background. Broader family financial or industry status not detailed in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early Facebook embedding, social platform wave, junior athletic discipline
evidence_summary: Morin joined Facebook in 2006 after Apple marketing and co-created Facebook Platform, launched May 2007 when he was 26—an independently reported product milestone (Wikipedia, contemporary tech press). Path (2010) and Slow Ventures came later. Family wealth and parental tech domain advantages are not documented; the main early advantage was immersion in the early Facebook ecosystem during the social-platform wave.
starting_point: Born 1980 in Helena, Montana; competitive junior skier who studied economics at CU Boulder before entering Apple marketing.
current_position: Entrepreneur and investor associated with Slow Ventures / Offline Ventures; Path co-founder; boards including Eventbrite historically; lives in Mill Valley, California.

trajectory.event: Graduated CU Boulder in economics and joined Apple in marketing.
Joined Facebook as senior platform manager after leaving Apple.
Co-created Facebook Platform, opening third-party applications inside Facebook.
Left Facebook and co-founded the private social network Path.
Helped launch immigration-advocacy group FWD.us with other tech leaders.
Started Offline Ventures, a VC firm using a subscription funding model.

name: Dmitri Alperovitch
milestone_by_age_26: Major public breakouts came later: Operation Aurora investigation (~2010, age ~30), Operation Shady RAT (2011), and co-founding CrowdStrike (late 2011, age ~31). Georgia Tech BS (2001) and first MS in information security (2003) are early credentials but not treated as independently material public milestones by age 26 under the strict bar.
early_history_summary: Born in Moscow (1980), emigrated via Canada to Tennessee in the mid-1990s; high-school encryption venture with physicist father; Georgia Tech CS BS/MS; CipherTrust/Secure Computing/McAfee threat research before co-founding CrowdStrike.
family_context_summary: Immigrant family from Russia; father Michael a nuclear physicist who worked at TVA after moving to Tennessee.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a nuclear physicist; father-son high-school encryption business noted in profiles, but not coded as age-26 eligibility milestone.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes profiles document birth year ~1980, Georgia Tech degrees through 2003, and later McAfee research leadership and CrowdStrike co-founding in 2011. No specific dated material public product, company, or research breakout verified at or before age 26.

name: Andrew Ng
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a Berkeley Ph.D. in computer science under Michael I. Jordan (2002/2003) and began as Stanford assistant professor in 2002 at age 26, after CMU BS, MIT MS, Bell Labs research, and building an early ML research-paper search engine.
early_history_summary: Born in London to Hong Kong immigrant parents (father a hematologist/UCL lecturer; mother arts administrator Tisa Ho), raised in Hong Kong and Singapore, and educated at Raffles Institution. Earned a CMU triple major (1997), MIT master's (1998), and Berkeley Ph.D. (thesis on shaping/policy search in RL), then joined Stanford faculty in 2002.
family_context_summary: Parents emigrated from Hong Kong; father Ronald Paul Ng was a hematologist and medical-school lecturer; mother Tisa Ho worked in arts administration. Family moved from London to Hong Kong then Singapore.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father practiced medicine and published early applied machine-learning work on medical diagnosis (Ng has cited a ~1980 paper); domain adjacency is partial (medicine/ML) rather than pure CS apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Raffles/CMU/MIT/Berkeley, Michael Jordan mentorship, Bell Labs research, professional family
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Ng’s CV, and institutional bios confirm Ph.D. and Stanford faculty start around age 26 after elite multi-institution training. Later Google Brain, Coursera, Baidu, DeepLearning.AI, Landing AI, and Amazon board roles amplify impact but are post-26. Family professional status and selective schools are documented; capital inheritance is not claimed beyond middle/professional class support.
starting_point: Born 1976 in London to Hong Kong immigrant professional parents; raised in Hong Kong and Singapore with selective schooling (Raffles Institution).
current_position: Founder of DeepLearning.AI; managing general partner of AI Fund; executive chairman of Landing AI; Coursera chairman/co-founder; Stanford adjunct professor; Amazon board member (from 2024).

trajectory.event: Earned CMU bachelor's with triple major in CS, statistics, and economics; conducted Bell Labs research.
Completed MIT master's and built an early automatically indexed web search engine for ML research papers.
Finished Berkeley Ph.D. under Michael I. Jordan and joined Stanford as assistant professor.
Founded and led Google Brain deep learning project; launched massively popular Stanford ML MOOC.
Co-founded Coursera with Daphne Koller, scaling free online education globally.
Became Baidu chief scientist, building large-scale AI research teams.
Left Baidu and launched DeepLearning.AI / Landing AI to democratize and industrialize AI.
Appointed to Amazon's board of directors amid generative-AI competition.

name: Werner Buchholz
milestone_by_age_26: Coined the term 'byte' in June 1956 at age 33 during IBM Stretch work; IBM 701 design contribution was also after age 26. No material dated computing milestone by age 26 verified (wartime displacement, University of Toronto and Caltech training occupied early adult years).
early_history_summary: Born 1922 in Detmold, Germany; fled antisemitism to England then was interned and sent to Canada; studied at University of Toronto and trained as an electrical engineer at Caltech; long IBM career in Poughkeepsie including 701 and Stretch.
family_context_summary: Son of merchant Julius Buchholz and Elsa Buchholz; Jewish family persecuted under Nazism; parents later murdered in Łódź/Litzmannstadt.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were merchants, not documented computer or engineering professionals.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and IBM Stretch historical memos place the coining of 'byte' in 1956 (age 33) and IBM pioneer recognition much later (IEEE Computer Pioneer Award 1990). Early adulthood was dominated by refugee/internment status and engineering education rather than a dated ≤26 industry milestone.

name: Reed Hastings
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Pure Software in 1991 at about age 30–31 and co-founded Netflix in 1997 at age 36–37. By age 26 (1986) he was between Peace Corps service (1983–85) and Stanford MS completion (1988)—no material founder/product milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Boston 1960 to a HEW attorney father and Boston Brahmin-lineage mother; Bowdoin math B.A. 1983; Peace Corps math teacher in Swaziland 1983–85; Stanford CS MS 1988; Adaptive Technology then Pure Software then Netflix.
family_context_summary: Father was a Department of Health, Education and Welfare attorney; mother from a Boston Brahmin family; maternal great-grandfather Alfred Lee Loomis.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family background is legal/government and elite social lineage rather than entertainment-tech domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, NYT, and Stanford Magazine place Pure Software founding ~1991 and Netflix 1997, both well after age 26. Stanford MS finished 1988 (~age 27–28). Strict age-26 bar not met despite later legendary success.

evidence_summary: Wikipedia and arXiv establish GANs (2014) and birth year 1987; MIT Technology Review and MIT Tech Review profiles confirm inventor status. early_history_summary: Born near San Jose 1983 to engineer parents; Bellarmine Prep; Rice University dual BA econ/CS 2005 and MS CS 2006; tutor marketplace while in college; IBM and Deloitte; Airbnb engineer 2011; Coinbase with Fred Ehrsam via YC 2012.
family_context_summary: Both parents were engineers; raised near San Jose, California.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were engineers, providing general technical environment rather than crypto-domain inheritance.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes confirm birthdate 1983-01-25 and Coinbase founding 2012 (~age 29). Education complete by ~23 but company-building breakout after 26; strict age-26 bar not met.
